subject: Biotechnology
title: Pharming: Drugs from Animals
description: One-minute skill: Pharming: Drugs from Animals.

hook.text: ATryn is a blood-clotting drug produced in goat milk — transgenic goats are pharmaceutical factories.

buildup.text: The human antithrombin gene fused to a milk-protein promoter — goats express the drug only in their mammary glands.

discovery.text: One transgenic goat produces more antithrombin in a year than a ton of human blood plasma could yield.

twist.text: Rabbit, chicken, and cow bioreactors also exist — each animal suits different protein sizes and volumes.

climax.text: Pharming avoids expensive bioreactors — the animal does the fermentation, purification still happens in the lab.

punchline.text: Goat milk as medicine — farming meets pharma.

quiz.question: How does ATryn production work in transgenic goats?
options: Goats are injected with the drug and their bodies amplify it
The human antithrombin gene is expressed in goat milk using a milk-protein promoter
Goats naturally produce antithrombin in their blood

details.summary: Pharming engineers livestock to produce pharmaceutical proteins in their milk, eggs, or blood. ATryn, purified from transgenic goat milk, was the first such drug approved. Animals serve as bioreactors for complex proteins that are difficult or impossible to produce in cell culture.
details.whyItMatters: A single transgenic goat can produce as much therapeutic protein in its milk as a large bioreactor, at a fraction of the capital cost.
takeaways: Transgenic animals produce pharmaceutical proteins in milk, eggs, or blood
ATryn from goat milk was the first pharmed drug approved by the FDA in 2009
Animal production can be cheaper and more scalable than cell culture bioreactors

faq.question: How do transgenic animals produce drugs in their milk?
faq.answer: The therapeutic protein gene is linked to a mammary gland-specific promoter like casein and inserted into the animal's genome. The protein is expressed exclusively in milk at concentrations of grams per liter. The drug is then purified from collected milk using standard biopharmaceutical methods.

faq.question: What are the ethical concerns about pharming animals?
faq.answer: Animal welfare concerns include the invasive procedures to create transgenic founders, potential health effects of expressing foreign proteins, and commodification of animals as manufacturing equipment. Regulatory frameworks require monitoring animal health throughout their productive lives.
